clue.text: In light rain the picture's identical

definitions.note: the answer is a noun phrase for an exact likeness; the clue uses it adjectivally

parts.note: when it is spitting, only a few drops of rain are falling
an image is a picture

explanation.surface: A painting of a drizzly scene looks exactly like the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is the spitting image of another person looks exactly like them, a near twin in appearance.

clue.text: Quiet room? It's a cliche

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
latitude is room for manoeuvre, freedom

explanation.surface: Asking for some peace and space is a well-worn request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' looks like a chamber, but here it means scope or freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark repeated so often it has lost force, which is what a cliche is.

clue.text: Animal in list Greg itemised on return

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Greg and the start of itemised

explanation.surface: A creature appears on a list that Greg itemised once he came home.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a large striped wild cat, one particular example of an animal.

clue.text: Fashionable rides, perhaps, for someone in the know

indicators.note: perhaps signals the word that precedes it might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: in means fashionable
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Trendy fairground rides suit a well-informed person.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is a member of a group with access to privileged information, someone who is well informed.

clue.text: Good women may wear them

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
lasses are young women

explanation.surface: Respectable ladies might put on spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and it also builds the answer piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses are spectacles worn on the face, which any women with poor eyesight may wear.

clue.text: Death rate inherent in the human condition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the frequency of deaths in a population
second meaning: the state of being bound to die

explanation.surface: Dying is built into what it means to be a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a statistic of deaths and the fact that every human being must eventually die.

clue.text: Range greater and more unusual than initially shown

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A selection proves bigger and stranger than at first appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The gamut is the complete scale or spectrum of something, its whole extent.

clue.text: Sam grasps a foe brutally in a fight

indicators.note: brutal treatment knocks things about, so the letters are roughed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sam savagely grabs an enemy during a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage of arms is a dated phrase for a combat or quarrel, a clash between opponents.

clue.text: Cooking appliance that's boy's pick — it's that or nothing!

parts.note: a hob is the cooking top of a stove
a son is a boy, with the possessive
a pick is a choice

explanation.surface: The kitchen stove is the lad's chosen one, take it or leave it.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob is the British word for the cooktop of a stove; the phrase comes from a Cambridge stable owner who offered customers only the horse nearest the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hobson's choice is a supposed option where only one thing is on offer, so take it or have nothing.

clue.text: Genial as a criminal getting painkiller

definitions.note: analgesia is the relief of pain rather than the drug itself

indicators.note: a criminal act is a wrong one, so the letters are put into a crooked order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly crook obtains some pain relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is medical relief from pain, the effect a painkilling drug produces; the clue loosely names the means for the result.

clue.text: Moore sculpture of a male lover

indicators.note: a sculpture is something shaped and moulded, so the letters are remodelled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Henry Moore statue depicts a man in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Moore was a famous English sculptor, which makes 'sculpture' read naturally as a description of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Romeo gives his name to any ardent man who courts women.

clue.text: Awful risk with English athlete

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English sportsman takes a terrible gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is a sportsperson who races or competes on snow slopes, an example of an athlete.

clue.text: French thinker sadly desecrates Edward's departing

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the remaining letters fall out of order
something departing leaves, so a letter goes out of the word it was in

parts.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the name stands for him

explanation.surface: A French philosopher regrettably defiles Edward's leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: One E (Edward's initial) leaves DESECRATES, and the nine letters left rearrange to DESCARTES.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was the seventeenth-century French philosopher of 'I think, therefore I am'.

clue.text: More flashy Spanish architect meets the Queen

parts.note: Antoni Gaudí designed the Sagrada Família in Barcelona
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A showier Spanish architect is introduced to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaudí's ornate buildings make 'more flashy' a neat fit for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy means showy or garish, so the comparative form describes something even more ostentatious.

clue.text: One student politician is reactionary

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car
a Liberal is a member of the Liberal party

explanation.surface: A particular campus activist turns out to be conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that a Liberal politician builds the word for an intolerant one.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means opposed to liberal ideas and freedoms, much like a reactionary stance against progress.

clue.text: Slip container into practice area

parts.note: to skid is to slip and slide
a pan is a cooking container

explanation.surface: Someone slides a box into a training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A skidpan is a slippery track where drivers practise controlling a skidding car.
explanation.definitionFit: A skidpan is a purpose-built slippery surface where drivers rehearse recovering from skids, hence a practice area.

clue.text: Chap on the beat is an American cop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man walking a regular patrol route
second meaning: the US term for a police officer on patrol

explanation.surface: A man walking his round is a US police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the beat' could suggest a musician keeping time, but a beat is a policeman's regular route.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a patrolman is a police officer of the lowest rank who walks or drives a set patrol.

clue.text: A plover distressed by time/space convergence?

indicators.note: distressed means battered or roughed up, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wading bird is upset by some cosmic collision of time and space.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: things overlap when they coincide in time or occupy the same space.
explanation.definitionFit: Two events or areas overlap when they partly coincide, sharing some of the same time or ground.

clue.text: Trap ape playing by a low wall

indicators.note: playing about with something means moving its parts freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey is caught while frolicking beside a garden wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective low barrier along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Puzzling call before soft muscular contraction

parts.note: a cry is a call or shout
p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
a tic is an involuntary twitch of a muscle

explanation.surface: Someone shouts just before a twitch of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means mysterious or obscure, so something cryptic is baffling and hard to understand.

clue.text: Seasoning accountant had fancy for not edible, originally

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a yen is a longing or fancy

indicators.note: originally points to how each of the last two words begins

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper wanted a spice for something that could not at first be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper powder used to spice and flavour food.

clue.text: Free article's bitterly misguided

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so the letters wander into another order

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece has been sharply and wrongly argued.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at liberty is to be unconfined and able to act as one likes, the same as being free.

clue.text: Relax and put up with the French first

indicators.note: first says that piece is placed at the front

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Take it easy and tolerate the French ahead of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like one phrase meaning tolerate, but it splits into a word, its reversal signal and a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To let up is to ease off or slacken one's efforts, much as one relaxes.

clue.text: Diagram deleted from the whole picture!

indicators.note: deleted from says one thing is struck out of a longer whole

parts.note: the full word for a photographic picture
a graph is a diagram of data

explanation.surface: Someone removes a chart from an overall image.
explanation.walkthrough: Take GRAPH off the end of PHOTOGRAPH and the short form PHOTO remains, which is itself a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Photo is the everyday shortening of photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Papa's strong desire to kill

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's joins it to the next part
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Father has a powerful longing to commit murder.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge a group is to get rid of opponents, often by having them executed.

clue.text: Mother — a term now rarely used

indicators.note: a term no longer in its usual use hints that its letters are put to another use

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The word for mum is described as old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue doubles as a description: mater is dated public-school slang for one's mother, and its letters also rearrange 'a term'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin for mother, once used jokingly by British schoolboys for their own mum.

clue.text: Roam around in great fear, getting an unbroken view of everything

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing such a view

indicators.note: turned around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order
in places one piece inside another

parts.note: panic is sudden great fear
the four letters shuffled

explanation.surface: A frightened wanderer scrambles to a vantage point that shows the whole scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' could be read as the container signal, but here it scrambles the word, and 'in' does the enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic outlook takes in a whole wide scene without interruption, like a panorama photograph.

clue.text: Drop article on vegetables and reveal a secret

parts.note: to spill is to let fall or drop
the is the definite article
beans are vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone drops an item onto the greens and blurts out a confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to disclose information that was meant to stay confidential.
